Declining solar radiation significantly affects maize growth at all growing stages, especially during grain filling and thus decreases grain yield21,22. Most researches have shown the effects of solar radiation on maize growth by conducting shading experi- ments13,21–23. Furthermore, different degrees and periods of shading have different effects on maize growth and development23. Previous studies had shown that shading caused maize grain yields to decrease significantly. In general, reductions in maize grain yields are greater with post-silking shading than before-silking shading21,24,25. Moreover, different maize genotypes show different responses to shading in terms of their growth and develop- ment. For maize varieties that are sensitive to weak light, the photosynthetic rate and fluorescence parameters of their leaves decrease greatly with shading, whereas varieties that are insensitive to weak light show only slight decreases in these two parameters. However, most previous studies were conducted in low solar radiation areas13, so any shading experiments performed in these areas would result in radiation levels below those that exist in any maize planting regions in China and other countries and therefore have little significance in real situations21–23. Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

P-19 MPT 2. Assessment of avoidable yield losses due to major diseases of maize The avoidable yield loss trials were conducted using paired plot technique with ten replications under sick plot/ artificial epiphytotic conditions. The avoidable yield losses were recorded up to 10.6-31.9 per cent due to TLB (Bajaura, Rahuri, Dharwad), 31.43-37.12 per cent due to BLSB (Karnal, Kalyani) and 47.07 per cent due to FSR (Kalyani) (Table no. 10-15). MPT 3. Trap nursery trial for disease incidence The trap nursery trial was conducted to find out the occurrence of disease and/or any new disease on a set of susceptible maize inbred lines at Almora, Bajaura, Coimbatore, Delhi, Dharwad, Dhaulakuan, Dholi, Hyderabad, Imphal, Karnal, Kalyani, Ludhiana, Mandya, Pantnagar, Peddapuram, Rahuri and Udaipur locations (Table no. 16-32). MPT 4. Disease survey and surveillance in different maize growing areas Survey and surveillance were done in the mandate maize growing areas of Bajaura, Coimbatore, Dharwad, Dhaulakuan, Dholi, Hyderabad, Imphal, Kalyani, Karnal, Ludhiana, Mandya, Pantnagar, Peddapuram, Rahuri and Udaipur centres. During survey and surveillance of diseases, scoring was carried out along with the disease incidence in prescribed proforma (Table no. 33-47). MPT 5. Efficacy of fungicides/chemicals in management of maize diseases Evaluation of newer fungicides/ chemicals were undertaken at Kalyani, Pantnagar, Dharwad, Mandya and Dholi for the management of FSR; BLSB; Common rust; Polysora rust; and BLSB disease, respectively. The results revealed that foliar spray of Fluopyrum 21.37% w/w + Trifloxystrobin 21.37%

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

With sufficient solar radiation, maize yields at the D3 planting density continued to increase. In contrast, yields at the D1 and D2 planting densities decreased as solar radiation increased. Several reasons could explain this phenomenon. On the one hand, when solar radiation is not a limiting factor, a high planting density can improve light interception; while at low planting densities, excessive solar radiation can result in photoinhibition and decreasing yields37. Therefore, within a narrow range, low planting densities can pro- duce higher yields than high planting densities under low solar radiation conditions14,36. Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

On the one hand, when solar radiation is not a limiting factor, a high planting density can improve light interception; while at low planting densities, excessive solar radiation can result in photoinhibition and decreasing yields37. Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.
